what: run_batch read an unreadable ASSAYS.json as {} and the first result overwrote every settled record.
how: Reproduced with a torn file. The resume read now retries 5 x 0.4 s (outwaits a reader or AV lock), then raises SystemExit naming the file and the error if it is still unreadable or not a dict. The file is never written. --fresh stays the only way to start from nothing. The running --calibrate process is untouched: calibrate() has its own reader, and run_batch changes only for batches started after this.

what: allsweep --quick lands ALLSWEEP.json with empty verifiers/estate, and consumers read it as a green full battery.
how: Confirmed at 910-1041. Not fixed: the full fix spans workorders.battery_faults and standards.py (not mine), and whether --quick may replace the battery artifact is audit Q2. Options: (a) --quick does not land ALLSWEEP.json and says so, which fails closed because the file then ages out; (b) stamp quick:true/tiers and have battery_faults/standards treat VERIFY/ESTATE as uncovered; (c) carry the previous full sweep's verifier/estate rows forward with their own timestamps.

what: The emanation cue `the One` matched ordinary 'the one who/that' under re.I.
how: The intent is clear from the code: it is the only capitalised cue, next to lowercase siblings, so it means the Plotinian One. It is now `(?-i:the One)`. Measured read-only on all records, old vs new: 12 sources move. Marvel emanation 1485 -> ex_nihilo 735, DC 830 -> ex_nihilo 506, Dragon Ball Z -> ex_nihilo, Soul Calibur -> eternal_cycle, Gears of War -> immanent, Who Framed Roger Rabbit -> immanent (15-15 tie). These go to ungrounded: all the Fate series, Ghost Recon, One Piece, Rosario + Vampire, StarCraft, the Lovecraftian mythos. Contested count goes 14 -> 8. data/GROUNDINGS.json was not rewritten; it changes only on the next `grounding.py --write`. Residual: capitalised 'the One Ring' / 'the One Above All' still count. The same-shape cues `the force`/`the weave`/`the current` are not measured and are left alone.

what: Guard 2's AXIS_LEXICON disagrees with feats.AXIS_ACT (28% of 'does not bear on' rejections are the generator's own candidates), and some stems are unanchored.
how: Not fixed (Hard Rule 3). Unifying the tables accepts more. Adding word boundaries is also not stricter overall: AXIS_RE is also guard 3(d)'s deed locator (subject_refusal: no match means the rival check is skipped) and quantity_scores' relevance test for the instrument override. So a narrower lexicon loosens guard 3. Options: (a) one table taken from feats._AXIS_ACT_RE, with an owner ruling on the accepted coverage gain; (b) word-anchor the stems only for guard 2 at verify:911, and keep the current AXIS_RE for subject_refusal and quantity_scores; (c) leave it, and document the split-vs-one-shot asymmetry.

what: host_ceiling returns None (read by callers as 'no ceiling, no clamp') on any non-ProbeUnread exception.
how: Verified. Not fixed: drill.py's existing net _net_efbfead57cb5 asserts `host_ceiling(...) is None` on exactly this path (the sweep67 ruling chose uncached None). Re-raising would BREACH that net, and I may not edit drill.py. Options: (a) re-raise like the ProbeUnread arm; run_batch.work already records the entity as a non-settled failure, so it is requeued. The coordinator updates that net to expect a raise; (b) return a sentinel that assay_entity refuses.

what: _resolve_citation resolved a long fabricated citation onto a short mined line it merely contained ('Speed', 'Ki' in 'killed').
how: Reproduced. In the numbered path, a pool whose single hit is not _substantial is now refused with a reason. Strictly stricter: exact equality still admits a short line quoted whole, and pools with two or more distinct lines were already refused. The split path (numbered=False) is unchanged.

what: _is_entity takes any span sharing one name token (Captain Marvel on Captain America's sheet) as the entity, so guard 3(d) misses the rival.
how: Verified. The audit's fix is stricter, but it over-refuses: _PROPER joins sentence-initial capitalised words, so 'Son Goku', 'Kid Goku', 'Super Saiyan Goku' and 'Enraged Goku ...' would all become rivals on Goku's own sheet, and coverage drops library-wide. That is a curatorial trade. Options: (a) the audit rule (every capitalised token in the span must be a form); (b) a rival only when the non-entity token is itself a catalogued name on the same host; (c) a title-word list (Captain/Doctor/Iron/Lord/...) that does not count as identity on its own.

what: The split path shows the anchor call raw model citations before any guard has checked them.
how: Code confirmed. Not run, because it needs a model. Reordering (gate first, then anchor over only the surviving citations) changes the anchor band both up and down, so it is not strictly stricter (Hard Rule 3). Options: (a) gate first and anchor on survivors; (b) keep the order and re-run the anchor when the gate drops any citation.

what: An exact two-way top tie (confidence 0.5) was classified by dict order and left off the contested list.
how: The contested test is now `<= 0.5`. The change is diagnostic only (the main() printout); no stored value changes.

what: _handler_is_observed credited a handler through a later `except ... as e` that rebinds the same name.
how: One-line change inside _block_reaches_sink's Try arm: each handler body is walked with its own bound name removed from the taint set. Signature unchanged. Measured with audit(), old vs new: 1405 sites, SILENT 364 -> 366; exactly drill.py:2325 and drill.py:22838 move to SILENT. No ratchet on the SILENT count was found.

what: problems() did not re-check TTL bounds or breadth on rows already in the file.
how: problems() now reports UNBOUNDED (non-finite, or expiring more than MAX_TTL_DAYS after added_at, or after now when added_at is missing) and BLANKET (a pattern made only of wildcards and slashes). Live SUPPRESSIONS.json still reports [].

what: convene accepted a NaN or out-of-range eta as a measured, non-vetoing curl.
how: convene now raises ValueError unless eta is None or a finite number in [0, 1]; None still abstains. The only callers pass 0.70 and 0.99, and anchors.py passes none. Added `import math`.

what: spine_code_for resolved a target contained in several index names at equal evidence by file order.
how: An equal-evidence tie between different codes now returns UNASSIGNED (Hard Rule 2). Checked old vs new on all 215 live roll names: 0 changes. 'Dragon' and 'Angels' now return UNASSIGNED.

what: grounding.main --write would land {} over GROUNDINGS.json when no record could be read.
how: main() now returns 1 and writes nothing when `out` is empty. Residual: a PARTIAL unreadable set still lands short. Counting record files cannot tell 'unreadable' from 'no entries' (6 live files have no entries); fixing that needs pipeline.records to report skips, which is not mine.

how: Owner ruling needed. Options: (a) keep them permanent; (b) stamp model and date and requeue when the model changes; (c) requeue after N days.

how: See F2.
